我是真不知道为什么这么多好评，打了3关+2个支线，目前玩下来游戏属实太简单了，还是杀戮尖塔那一套，唯一增加难度的点是过事件解救囚徒会强制往卡组里塞基本用不上的垃圾卡，再就是跳过选牌扣30金也算是个增加难度的点。 这游戏回血牌很多，又没有回合限制，打怪掉血随便留个菜鸡怪刷血就行能一直保证满血，甚至不嫌麻烦香肠也能刷。 卡池太浅了，能构筑的空间属实有限，怪物种类也少，拢共20多种怪，那个升级给属性点+属性真的意义不明，我打了3关升了2级给了6个属性点，6属性点才加1攻击力，这意思是打不过的时候可以去简单的关卡练级？问题是打起来真的是太无聊了，实在是没刷的动力啊。

这游戏问题很大，玩过枪与香蕉的玩家都能感觉出来这游戏大量借鉴枪与香蕉，甚至把一些缺点也搬了过来。比如枪与香蕉不能跳过选卡，是一个很烂的设计，它就改成可以花30跳过选卡，但是我打一个1级怪才给十几块钱，打2级怪也才30块钱左右，相当于我跳过了这关就白打了，再加上卡池里有很多烂卡、凑数卡，很多时候只能为了留点钱捏着鼻子三选一选个不那么烂的，降低卡组质量（删卡要25哦，删第二张要50，等差数列）。还有局外成长，非常抽象，一个角色4级到5级要12000经验，但是一次战斗只给100多经验，我5个小时都在玩初始角色都没升到5级。升级只给3个属性点，要6属性点才能+1伤害，9属性点+1抽卡，这数值得要玩家多肝？用肝来掩饰设计的贫瘠。还有食物的设定，比枪与香蕉的还烂，初始100，初始卡组一般消耗20-30，因为经常不会跳过选卡，消耗就越来越大，好在没食物了损失也不大，只是随机一张卡不能用，这个设计几乎可以说是毫无意义。

还没有完全优化好游戏机制，甚至连地图做的也让人稀里糊涂，不建议购买
好玩 ，但是香肠花费太多，影响升级小矮人卡牌，建议每前进一次，香肠减少点

《打倒白雪公主！乌拉！》是一款黑童话背景的DBG卡牌构筑游戏，联合一众矮人同胞，对抗催眠洗脑抹黑压榨矮人们的邪恶女魔头——白雪公主！整体多地图、短章节的关卡形式，虽说EA阶段内容尚不完全，但已经具有9张地图，每章节都有一定的剧情演绎，击败每章节的公主爪牙、解放同胞、解锁更多矮人卡牌，一步一步逼近邪恶公主的老巢！ [h1] 借鉴了《枪与香蕉》，且目前内容不足、较为单调[/h1] 作为DBG卡牌构筑游戏，不可避免谈到一个对象，那就是杀戮尖塔，不过，整体游玩下来，其实本作更多是学习借鉴了《枪与香蕉》。费用、卡牌、拿牌机制都接近，费用不会自动回复，需要在卡组里填充一些0费卡或者补充魔法的卡牌，卡牌具有近远程的区分，不抓牌要付出代价，以及最为明显的酒醉、闪避、目盲等50%随机概率的buff。 整体本作也有自个儿的创新，像是新颖的黑童话背景、亮眼的画风、独特的故事冒险关卡，都赋予了本作别样的风格与趣味，但在如今EA阶段，由于英雄就俩，卡池也不深，以及每章节短关卡的形式下，卡组成长性较低、构筑空间有限，或多或少也放大了游戏的缺点，显得有些体验单调了！ [h1] 短章节模式下，策略性调整初始卡组[/h1] 目前，游戏一共8张地图，都是9-17步通关的短章节关卡形式下；并且，玩家打完一张地图、之后就再次拿回基础卡组、重新打下一张地图，因此不可避免地造成了卡组成长性有限，尤其是本作还大胆地删除了遗物、消耗品的构筑内容，取而代之的是重复游戏刷经验、提升角色等级、属性、点天赋。 好消息是游戏中，玩家可以自己更换初始卡组的构筑，挑选任意10张牌往里面塞；且每张地图长度与特色各异，除了5张具有各异关卡buff的爬塔路线选择地图，还有3个类似剧本杀的故事冒险、1个连续50场战斗的无尽噩梦关卡，使得玩家能够根据每个章节的特点进行卡组的调整，富有策略的进行卡牌搭配。 以及另一方面的策略性来源，便是对抗系统上的恶意、保证卡组的完整性与纯洁性，一方面，地图上走格子的消耗会消耗资源“香肠”，一旦香肠为0则每走一格都会有一张随机卡牌饿晕过去、无法使用；另一方面，跳过选牌每次也需要花30块，一些牢房更是会强制往卡组里塞人，有时就不得不被污染卡组。 [h1] 除内容不足外的负面体验部分[/h1] 坏消息是目前这个等级与属性系统意义不明，一方面，是如今升级所需经验多的有些离谱，另一方面是数值和策略性本身就难免有些冲突，一旦真要刷数值，游戏的策略性肯定大幅降低，毕竟我刷个100%闪避、100%暴击，请问阁下又该如何应对。以及后续游戏，即便有什么难度设计不合理也可以往数值上推拖。体验较为负面。 “香肠”机制目前也比较鸡肋。虽说既能用于英雄的主动技能释放，又算是一定程度增加了游戏的难度or策略性，但由于每步扣的香肠太多、使得这个机制完全没法策略性的应对，只是被动的压迫玩家、不断抓牌以及面对随机昏迷。对于我这种从不精简卡组的懒人而言，倒是完全无所谓，但反正也说不上趣味性就是了。 并且暴击卡组只要塞一张暴击+香肠的卡，即可完全无视“香肠”机制，因为虽说暴击只+6香肠，但只要香肠不为0、即便低于卡组的每步消耗，也不会有人饿晕过去。 [h1]总结[/h1] 面对短章节关卡的初始卡组调整、有趣的故事冒险模式算是本作卡牌玩法上的亮点，但目前卡牌内容不算充足，体验还比较单调；可以观望一下再入手尝试。 [quote]加入[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/GHYX]干货游戏[/url]&关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/35106417/]咱的鉴赏家[/url]，不定期为大家带来游戏体验分享，也期待您来一起分享自己的游戏体验干货~[/quote]
香肠跟金币问题，实际上可以通过事件获得资源解决， 香肠不足 小矮人饥饿时候会丧失战斗能力，但是获得一次香肠后，又恢复正常了 所以尽量在boss前一关补充香肠 但是你tmd的那个傻卵局外成长 我现在七级 升一级要四万五 然后你给我三点技能点 加的那点破属性加了跟没加一样 更别提你的牌了 表面上94张 实际用的不超过20张 很多玩法看得到思路 组建不了 建议一年后等正式版再入手

[h1]在暗黑童话中打败白雪公主[/h1] 近期的卡牌类新游是真的多，层出不穷。这款《打倒白雪公主！乌拉！》则在各个方面都制作精良，暗黑童话风格的剧情也相当吸引人。在这款俄罗斯人制作的游戏中，白雪公主变成了西方邪恶的化身，她的能力也在原有的基础上进行了黑化，白雪公主拥有奴役小矮人的能力，抓捕并将小矮人们奴役起来。在白雪公主的压迫统治下，矮人们的生活困苦不堪。但他们没有屈服，反而在酝酿着伟大的革命。工人们、农民们、矿工们——伟大的无产主义矮人战线正在联合起来，准备打破枷锁，迎接新的黎明。游戏中处处充满了暗黑童话的剧情和内容，什么狼外婆啊，巫婆骑士啊，都会在游戏中出现。 [h1]规划小矮人部队的进攻路线[/h1] 游戏中玩家带领着反抗的小矮人们向着城堡进发，在路途中还需要击败那些试图阻挡我们的敌人。游戏采用了传统爬塔式的三线进攻模式，玩家需要规划好自己的前进路线，以便规划在后面碰到的格子。与传统的爬塔游戏不同的是，本作中拥有一个食物资源，每次小矮人部队移动的时候都会消耗食物，而消耗的多少取决于玩家小矮人部队的阵容，玩家在初期可以规划自己的初始部队，在前进的过程中，还会在战斗结束后收编一些被解放的小矮人，也会在一些特殊的格子招募到新的单位。而随着队伍小矮人的壮大，每次移动消耗的食物也会增多。如果没有及时补充食物，则每次移动都会有一个小矮人被饿晕，导致无法在战斗中发挥其作用，只有在补充了足够的食物后才能恢复。 [h1]核心的卡牌玩法[/h1] 游戏的核心玩法还是卡牌玩法，除去规划小矮人的移动路径，管理食物与金钱的资源外，最主要的还是战斗部分。本作的战斗采用的就是卡牌的玩法，每个小矮人都是一张卡牌，有自己独特的作用和消耗。每个回合会在卡组中随机抽取卡牌，部分卡牌打出是没有消耗的，也有卡牌会需要消耗魔法，初始玩家拥有3点魔法，每个回合也会回复1点，上限3点。另外卡牌也有很多说明，针对不同的目标也会产生不同的作用，根据卡牌使用的顺序不同也会造成不同的效果。游戏中小矮人的种类非常丰富，卡牌效果组合也异常丰富，打牌的玩法内容不错，具有很强的策略性。 [table][td][b]欢迎关注我们 [/b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/10591434/]突突突发糖辣！[/url] [/td][/table]
卡通风格，动画表现非常棒，角色鲜活可爱。具有话题性的反英雄主题。 每次旅行（爬塔）流程不长，打完可以重新整备，玩起来不那么累。 战斗明快，操作流畅节奏快。构筑卡牌的同时还要注意行军粮储备。 矮人不止7只，而是种类和数量都很多，并且一个个都很会颜艺。 游戏中还融入了一些网络梗。 各方面都让人感觉轻松有趣的游戏。

I am really enjoying this game, It’s funny, bright but charming. You have a hero gnome (your character archetype) that leads a wagon of gnomes (your deck) that you will move along the map within a traditional Rogue type map but with a twist. You gotta manage your wieners! Yup, you gotta feed those little guys and they consume wieners. So you balance team strength with wiener consumption and that adds an interesting layer of gameplay at the map level. Inside combat you see all the familiar mechanic with an added layer of wieners that you can also spend for big perks or buff but that can also mean you come up short on feeding your gnomes, so what does that mean? Every time you move one gnome in your caravan will faint and be unusable for the next combat and then return to active. This cycle continues until you obtain more wieners. I think it’s a fair system but opinions seem split on this mechanic. This is currently a k/m game but there is a downloadable community control support accessible through the steam control layouts screen. If you’re a Steam Deck user you have the added functionality of the touchscreen allowing you to play this like a tablet game. I did this for a full play through and it worked flawlessly. At this point in its EA phase it seems to be a pretty well fleshed out game with a solid foundation to start on. I’ve had minor graphic hick ups, 2 lag moments that lasted about 5 seconds and no crashes, with 4 and half hours of game time at the time of this review. TLDR: Games funny, musics mid, combat is solid, they bring and interesting layer of gameplay with their wiener mechanics. Runs great on Steam Deck out of the box. This Gn0m3 BUY!

[quote][h1] 从细节处入手，撬动失败的天平[/h1][/quote] 看似如此多的卡牌类游戏，其实只要我们体验后还是发现基本都是杀戮like，《打到白雪公主》这款游戏体验下来也是不例外的，整个游戏的节奏、战斗规则基本都是脱胎于杀戮尖塔，将其称之为变种的杀戮尖塔其实并不为过，但具体而言这款游戏仅仅是有形而无神。 正如开头所言杀戮like的游戏实在太多，如果有什么值得一说的可能就是游戏的背景设置成了一个饭童话吧，游戏的BOSS并不是邪恶的女巫而是传统意义上的白雪公主。 在游戏内玩家手牌的招式替换为了各式各样的小矮人，这种小矮人同样按照功能划分为了进攻、防御、辅助三大类，而按照消耗划分则是分为是否消耗能量，你以为游戏的变量是从这个细节出发的吗？ 但实际上只要打完几把你就可以感觉到游戏真正恶心玩家地方是每次战胜敌人后制作组都以近乎强制的方式在玩家手中塞牌，对比杀戮尖塔来说玩家战胜后不仅可以选择不接受新的卡牌还能获得一笔金钱奖励，但这个游戏中你不接受牌反而要扣你的钱？ 这是什么操作？就因为所谓的牌在游戏内是小矮人我不救他们就要给他们一笔安家费吗？什么道理这是。 长远来说，这种模式直接让此类游戏中一种经典打法流派直接报废，随着战斗推进我们只能选择茫茫多的垃圾卡牌去战斗，如果运气不好抽到不堪可用的卡牌，那么不好意思！这绝对是你的打牌技术不够，不能利用好每张卡牌，而绝不是制作组的垃圾设计有问题！ 至于每场战斗都需要消耗香肠的设计我都不想说了，这种细节处的改变如果能够运用好是能够撬动胜利的天平，但运用不好就是自作聪明了。 这款游戏是什么水平，我不再多说。 [table] [tr] [th]游戏由SteamPY鉴赏家提供[/th] [/tr] [tr] [td]SteamPY鉴赏家[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td][h3]上SteamPY淘海量超低价游戏[/h3][/td] [/tr] [/table]

[h1] A Card Game KING review [/h1] Union of Gnomes introduces a few new novelties compared to other roguelike deckbuilders that all hit differently. Well, let's start with the roguelike part. The game isn't quite a roguelike, as it has sort of a campaign, but dying will only reset the current mission attempt, not your overall progress. Outside of that, there are permanent upgrades which make the game easier over time. In the flood of roguelike games, it's nice to see an island where you can take it a bit easier and I quite liked the change of air. The other novelties that the game introduces are not my favorite unfortunately. Wieners are a resource that you spent on moving, and temporary lose cards if you don't have enough. But you will never have enough so sometimes you will lose a strong card right before a big battle. You can also use them for active abilities (like permanently available potions) which was far more fun, but barely had the resources to use them. The other mechanic I didn't quite enjoy is tying mana to cards. I always thought that was the biggest downside of MTG, and the game shares the same pain points. Sometimes you won't draw mana cards when you need them, sometimes you will draw too much of them. Unfortunately, mana cards are also rare for some reason, making it even more difficult to support mana hungry decks. Thankfully mana stays between turns, so it's slightly more manageable. Overall, the game feels fine: the animations of gnomes are fun, the gameplay solid and the setting unique. However, the wiener and mana systems are more fiddly than fun, there aren't very interesting card combos and it doesn't feel like there are a lot of interesting choices to make. One example, is that after battles you get more cards, but in order not to take a card you have to pay with gold (other games usually compensate you). When all of the cardchoices are bad, this means the choice is between making a worse deck or making a worse deck (as I could spend gold on upgrades). Not a fan of that. Overall, it's a solid entry but some systems feel like they could seriously be tinkered with. [h1][b]The positive[/b] [/h1] + Silly Gnome animations. + Solid gameplay. + No big loss of progress on loss and a campaign style game with permanent upgrades to heroes. [h1][b]The neutral[/b][/h1] * Wish there were more exciting combos to play with. [h1][b]The negative[/b][/h1] - A mana system that's tied to cards comes with all of its drawbacks. - Wieners feel encumbering. Yes, I will leave it at that. [h1][b]Conclusion:[/b] [/h1] Promising game with solid foundations, but currently lacks fun combos and has problematic mana and wiener mechanics. Careful recommendation for now. [h1]另类童话故事[/h1] 童话故事总是美好的，但当故事中的白雪公主变成邪恶的一方，老巫婆也不过是她手底下可有可无的将领时，故事又将如何继续？《打倒白雪公主！乌拉！》就是这么一款游戏，游戏中玩家将扮演被压迫已久的小矮人一方，在英雄的带领下反抗白雪公主的统治。游戏采用的是卡牌肉鸽的玩法，但是我们手中的卡牌其实代表的是小矮人的军队，玩家将作为这支军队的英雄，在一个个关卡中击败白雪公主的手下，最后推翻她的统治，为小矮人们带来自由。 [h1]玩法[/h1] 游戏采用了线性关卡制，每一关都是肉鸽爬塔的卡牌玩法，不过在选择关卡和爬塔之前，玩家拥有一个大本营，可以在这里提升自己的英雄属性，替换自己的小矮人阵容（卡组）。而游戏除了正常的主线章节内容以外，还拥有许许多多的外传任务，完成之后可以获得更多的小矮人（卡牌）。而完成主线章节也可以获得新的卡牌，同时也会解锁新的英雄。 [h1]矮人们[/h1] 游戏中的小矮人分为近战和远程，近战小矮人只能攻击前排敌人，远程小矮人可以攻击任意位置的敌人，这一点在战斗中还是需要注意的，因为游戏中有相当多的效果是分远程和近战的，使用时需要注意。 [h1]干饭是第一生产力[/h1] 游戏在关卡中最重要的一项无非就是香肠了，香肠就相当于军粮，游戏中玩家卡组中的每张小矮人卡牌都会有对应所需的香肠数量，每次移动时都要消耗卡组总和的香肠数量，一旦香肠数量不够，就会有小矮人饿昏过去，即该卡牌在战斗中无法使用。除此之外，香肠还可以在战斗中释放一些技能，比如说该回合魔法卡不耗魔法、护盾值转化为生命值、对所有敌人造成伤害。 [h1]这个世界需要更多的英雄[/h1] 游戏中英雄的升级采用的是经验值系统，玩家在完成关卡任务后会获得经验值，通过经验值提升等级后会获得天赋点和属性点，依靠这两个点数可以分别升级英雄的天赋和属性值，这对于游戏的战斗还是起到很大作用的。玩家初始只拥有一个射手英雄，在通关第二章后会解锁第二个战士英雄，两个英雄的侧重点不同，总之玩法相当多样。 [h1]最后来点碎碎念和总结[/h1] 游戏的外传模式其实还是相当有趣的，正确的选择可以帮助玩家规避很多战斗，从而轻松的通过外传获取奖励。游戏的整体玩法还是相当有意思的，特别是把卡牌变成军队还需要一定的军粮这个想法。不过也正是因为如此，玩家在游戏中要实时关注自己的军粮变化，不然晕倒两张不重要的卡牌还好，一旦晕倒的是比较核心的卡牌那只能指望自己命大了。总来讲还是一款相当出色且想法奇特的卡牌游戏，很推荐喜欢卡牌的玩家尝试一下。 [quote]点击关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/41448772//]三言两语评测」→ [/url]简洁的语言，实用的内容 [/quote]

[h1] 这不是肉鸽！这不是肉鸽！这不是肉鸽！ [/h1] [h2] 轻度玩家可考虑，资深牌佬勿入 [/h2] 标签定位就有问题，这个游戏的模式根本就不能算肉鸽。没有永久死亡，打法其实说白了就是下一个个副本（地牢），副本可以反复打刷属性，死亡或者打完副本后回到营地，分明是更传统的地牢探索加了个卡牌玩法。虽然说肉鸽这个概念确实现在被扩大化了很多，但也不能随便啥模式都叫肉鸽吧。[b]你这要叫肉鸽，难道你们管大菠萝也叫肉鸽？[/b] 和现在主流肉鸽卡牌构筑完全不是一个定位，玩的根本不是单局游戏（a run），而是一个个副本串下来的整个流程（a campaign）。 然后卡牌构筑方面来说，初见感觉玩法还挺新颖，但是实际多打两把就发现卡牌构筑的策略性很弱，基本上就是纯打数值。每走一格都要补给的设定玩起来没有爽快感，而且还半强制拿牌（不拿-30），然后拿了牌补给越掉越快。虽然理论上是有卡可以刷香肠，但每局战斗都苟回复刷香肠那也太无聊了吧。 这一类玩法看起来很新颖，其实策略性非常弱的卡牌构筑最近真的已经见过太多了（我都至少买过10+以上这种卡牌游戏了）。基本特点都是每回合裸摸5牌，弱化回合内抽牌效果，弱化局内拿牌删牌的策略，最后导致的结果都是从牌组成型到战斗内抽牌都是纯看脸，突出一个纯打数值。问题是数值又特别抠抠搜搜的，完全爽不起来。真的不让转纯靠数值但依然好玩的卡牌游戏不是没有，但人家要么就是机制是有足够颠覆性的新颖（不是这个游戏看起来新但其实本质换汤不换药的），要么是成功构筑一个卡组以后数值膨胀到非常爽，能带给玩家足够成就感的。你这又不够新，还不给爽，那真的就是不好玩。 然后局外成长的设计也特别离谱，升6个技能点才能点+1攻，打完三个本才点出一个+1。先不说这种纯刷子设定，你这前期一点正反馈都不给玩家，真的会有玩家去刷吗？

Would not recommend at it's current state. The humor is fine, the card game isn't that bad... the two major issues are. 1) The Bird enemy. when you face any encounter that has three birds most of the time you will lose. This is made worse as NORMAL ENCOUNTERS past the second stage can have you face two birds which can then spam the field with 3 birds easily since there are only two enemies... and you have RNG to determine if you have the cards needed to win. 2) The food resource... it is hard to get, hard to deal with, and made worse since most of the Bird Advice is to use the wagon cannons... which requires food to work... and no Food = no cannons. Every fight adds a gnome to your part upping the food cost unless you pay 30 gold to reject the gnome. Food has to be bought costing 25 coins... unless you gained the one ranged card that on a crit adds 6 food. Part of the reason why the Ranger for the gnomes is considered a main as you need to try making the infinite food loop of not harming an enemy except by crit rang food harvest attack. Though even a 20 food cost starting army can easily hit 50 food cost near the end of the map... so if you run into birds that means your deck clogged down from random cards can prevent you from winning... against three birds when you could have actually defeated the boss instead of facing the never ending and always looping bird swarm. Maybe it gets 'easier' with more cards... but the fact the birds keep making the game worse... means they either need a nerf, the food gathering needs a buff, or there needs to be a guide that can actually explain how to get past them least RNG is the only thing determining if you are lucky in avoiding the birds to beat the boss or if you lost another run because of the infinite bird enemy blockade. This is early access and while it has some fun ideas... it has two major problems... and the birds compound the issue since they are a common foe that can appear on every map.

I'll say that I enjoy the game. I think the design is nice, humor is good and it has some positives in the card system. However, the food system is horrible... you need food to move or you lose gnome cards out of your deck, but food also allows you to cast your special abilities, which are pretty necessary on some of these fights. They put birds in that have no cap in how many can summon like in other Roguelike Deckbuilders, so unless you get the exact amount of damage with crystals to use you are sitting in an infinite cycle of spawn summons. It gets tedious. It causes you to use your special abilities that cost food which is already at a premium to then get closer to zero food where you start losing gnome cards out of your deck. I really hope the developers either fix the food system by giving you much more food to start, removing food as a currency to move forward on the map, or just remove the food system all together. I do recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun roguelike deckbuilder. However I am going to mark it as a "No" so that the devs receive this feedback and fix the mechanics plaguing it. I will update my rating if that changes. Update: I said I'd come back if the game was updated and the sausage system was fixed and it hasnt been perfected, but it is better than it was and with some rebalances that were done the game is worth a purchase for anyone that wants a fun deckbuilder. Thumbs up.

这款肉鸽卡牌游戏改变了原有的童话故事人设，小矮人们需要团结起来，在英雄的带领下打到白雪公主。游戏的美术风格属于Q般搞笑风格，每种小矮人兵种带的技能就是卡牌的能力，每回合可以抽取五张卡牌进行战斗，车上的矮人可以消耗金币或者香肠主动发动能力。不同的英雄和小矮人可以组成强力有趣的流派，关卡类型则有点像杀戮尖塔，三条路线交叉最终抵达关卡boss。 游戏有两种资源消耗，香肠和金币。香肠相当于粮草，队伍前进和雇佣矮人都会消耗香肠，金币可以用来购买香肠和回复健康以及强化卡牌。值得注意的是。战斗胜利会强制给牌，如果不要的话会扣金币，尽量不要选择与原本构筑完全不相关的卡牌，或者在后面花费金币删除卡牌。 推进剧情可以获得新英雄，英雄升级会获得属性和天赋加成，比如第一个英雄的破盾后加2层闪避，就可以利用回合结束不会掉盾量的设定卡这个闪避加成，有着很不错的战斗体验。

It’s a mix of deckbuilding, tactical battles, and dungeon-crawling, with a fairy-tale-gone-wrong theme. Each run, you build your deck while exploring a randomly generated map, collecting resources, and upgrading your wagon. It is enough of a twist to keep it interesting while keeping the meat and potatoes of card battler in place. The uniqueness comes from the exploration part, since rather than nodes (that are present in the story mode), you explore the map with resources (food). It’s sort of Roguebook or even Darkest Dungeons-style, although admittedly not that hard. But it’s a fun new layer of the gameplay where you need to search for the boss first and the path to them but you are also free to wander around the map and backtrack to gather more resources/artifacts before moving forward.

This is what happens when Slay the Spire, Darkest Dungeon, and a fairy tale fever dream collide at high speed. I didn’t expect much. But turns out, managing your sausage rations while commanding a wagon of tiny anarchists through cursed forests is… oddly therapeutic? Combat is tight. Positioning matters. So does resource planning. It’s not just a comedy game - there’s legit strategy here. The variety of cards and interactions surprised me. You’ll fail a few runs early on, but once you learn to work with modifiers and wagon upgrades, it clicks. Can’t wait to see what they add next. Highly replayable and refreshingly original. Would I recommend it? If you've ever wanted to overthrow a fairy tale regime with cards and gnome rage: yes. Yes, you should.

IMO everything about this game is great, except balance and translation. The balance issues make the game frustrating. The loading screen suggestion of try changing your squad in camp is insulting. You might be 45 minutes into an otherwise successful run and then you randomly hit a group of enemies that have some combination of abilities that your deck can not overcome. Changing your squad literally means starting over and wasting another 45 minutes. Progressing in the campaign means 1) you've setup a decent deck and 2) RNG was in your favor or 3) you have tried and failed enough that meta-progression has offset RNG enough to eek out a win. Compared to something like Slay the Spire. In STS, as the player, you always feel like you are in control. Even if you have RNG setbacks, you know that your greed vs safe choices led you to your position. In UOG you don't have that type of control, RNG just has too much weight to the outcome. There are no greed vs safe choices to evaluate. Most of the choice you can make are trial and error sequence based. If you've seen the event before and you memorized a successful sequence you repeat it, otherwise you are going in blind and the choice is literally click "go left" or "go right". The translation issues seem to be pretty rare are really not that bad, but they do make understanding the rules of the game more confusing. IMO this game needs balance polish, until then, for me personally, its too frustrating to put time into.

This game made some design decisions that I find hard to understand. You start with a deck of 10 gnomes, and then have the ability to add more throughout each run. But the gnomes you start out with are no less powerful then the ones you find along the way, so unlike StS you aren't making your deck stronger by adding new cards; you are just diluting it and pivoting somewhat. Furthermore, you have to pay upkeep for each gnome in your deck. It is a very thematic rule, but mechanically it makes adding more cards have an even larger drag. Combined with needing to upgrade gnomes individually, the end result is that increasing your squad is liable to make you weaker, not stronger.

A dull card game with major flaws and a very bad campaign mode. In the campaign missions you can't skip adding cards to your deck and you have to pay travel costs based on card value (which is irritating in its own right). You're forced to dilute your deck and then are penalized for doing so. The deck manager is horrible. There's no search option, storage doesn't put returned cards in order so they're all jumbled, the filters are so limited as to be useless, and you can't save decks. Some mission bosses have strengths that completely negate certain decks. If you encounter a poison immune boss, you'll have to trash your poison deck then build a different one then afterwards rebuild your poison deck, all while fighting the terrible deck building UI. Adding insult to injury, missions don't warn you what the boss's strength is so you might spend an hour getting to the end of a map just to find your deck can't damage the boss at all. The only thing that changes how your deck functions during a mission is "bling" that you can use to add bonuses to card slots. Unfortunately they only last 1 mission, they rarely drop, and you have to get lucky to draw a card into the bling slot that meets the bonus's often very limited criteria. The roguelite mode is significantly better - the deck editor is blissfully unnecessary, the movement penalty is handled differently, and blings are a little more impactful since you get more and the runs are longer. Unfortunately that just exposes how uninteresting the gameplay is - block, attack, buff, debuff, mana, health, it's all bog standard. Once you lock down a good build every battle feels the same which is a big problem given that runs last well over an hour. With numerous design flaws, lack of interesting mechanics, and heavy grind, there's no reason for anyone to consider this one.

"When a Fairytale Adventure Feels More Like a Bedtime Story." At first, I was honestly very intrigued by the premise of Union of Gnomes. A roguelike deckbuilder with a gnome-focused world mixed with fairy tale elements sounded genuinely unique, especially for a genre that often repeats the same dark fantasy or sci-fi themes. The concept and setting immediately caught my attention, and as someone who loves roguelike deckbuilders, I expected this to be something I’d really get into. Unfortunately, in my short time playing it, I was surprised by how quickly the game lost my interest. Despite being fairly straightforward mechanically, the overall pacing felt oddly slow and dragged down the experience for me. Even shorter runs somehow felt like a slog to get through, which is the opposite of what I usually want from this genre. There’s constantly a lot happening on screen and within the systems, but instead of feeling engaging, it mostly just felt tiring. The biggest issue by far for me was the loading times. They were honestly insanely bad for a single-player roguelike deckbuilder and completely killed the flow of the game. It’s very unusual for games in this genre to struggle that much with loading, so every delay felt even more noticeable and frustrating. That ended up becoming my biggest gripe overall because it made the entire experience feel less responsive and far slower than it should have been. The presentation also didn’t fully land for me either. The art style feels inconsistent at times, almost like certain visual elements belong to completely different games and don’t blend together naturally. On top of that, the music is very mellow and low-energy, which only added to the sluggish feeling the game already had during runs. To be fair, there’s clearly a lot of content and ideas packed into the game, and I can see some players appreciating the slower pace and unique setting. But personally, I just couldn’t stick with it long enough to really enjoy what it was trying to do. Ultimately, this ended up being one of my least favorite roguelike deckbuilders I’ve played in quite a while, which is disappointing because the premise had a lot of potential.

Union of Gnomes is a refreshing blend of roguelike deckbuilding and tactical strategy that takes familiar fairy-tale concepts and turns them upside down. Developed by Hoolignomes and published by HeroCraft PC, the game places players in charge of a rebellion of gnomes determined to overthrow the oppressive rule of Snow White. This unusual premise immediately gives the game a distinctive identity, separating it from many fantasy-themed deckbuilders that often rely on more conventional heroes-versus-monsters narratives. The result is a colorful and entertaining adventure that combines humor, strategic combat, and meaningful progression into a surprisingly engaging package. The game's story serves as more than a simple backdrop for battles. Players guide a growing resistance movement through a world inspired by classic fairy tales, encountering familiar characters and locations that have been reimagined through a comedic lens. The writing embraces satire and playful humor, creating an atmosphere that remains lighthearted even when the stakes become serious. Rather than presenting a dark revolution, the game delivers a whimsical struggle for freedom that consistently maintains its charm. The narrative may not be overly complex, but it provides enough personality and motivation to keep players invested throughout their campaign. Combat is where Union of Gnomes truly shines. The game follows the foundations of the roguelike deckbuilding genre while introducing its own tactical twists. Instead of controlling a single protagonist, players command a squad of gnomes, each contributing unique strengths and abilities to the battle. This party-focused design encourages experimentation and strategic planning, as success depends not only on the cards in a deck but also on how effectively the team works together. Every encounter requires players to balance offense, defense, resource management, and status effects, creating a satisfying level of depth that rewards careful decision-making. The card system is one of the strongest aspects of the experience. A large selection of cards allows players to build highly specialized strategies centered on damage output, poison effects, debuffs, support abilities, or complex combinations of multiple mechanics. Discovering powerful synergies becomes one of the game's most rewarding elements, especially during longer runs where a carefully crafted deck begins to showcase its full potential. The variety available ensures that different playthroughs rarely feel identical, encouraging players to test new approaches and adapt to changing circumstances. Like any successful roguelike, Union of Gnomes thrives on replayability. Randomized encounters, evolving deck options, and unpredictable rewards create a sense of discovery that keeps runs engaging even after multiple attempts. Defeat is an expected part of the experience, but each failure provides valuable lessons that improve future performance. The progression system successfully balances challenge and reward, motivating players to continue refining their strategies and pushing deeper into the game's content. This loop of experimentation and improvement forms the foundation of the game's long-term appeal. Another noteworthy feature is the emphasis on resource management and strategic choices outside of combat. Players must carefully decide how to navigate their journey, weighing potential rewards against the risks of future encounters. Recruiting new allies, upgrading capabilities, and conserving valuable resources all contribute to a greater sense of planning. These decisions add another layer of depth that extends beyond the battlefield and help make each run feel unique. Visually, the game embraces a bright and whimsical art style that complements its fairy-tale setting. Character designs are expressive and memorable, while environments successfully capture the playful nature of the world. The presentation may not rival larger-budget productions, but it effectively communicates the game's tone and keeps battles easy to read. Combined with fitting sound design and a lively atmosphere, the visual presentation helps bring the world of rebellious gnomes to life. Union of Gnomes succeeds because it combines familiar roguelike deckbuilding mechanics with a creative setting and strong tactical foundations. Its humorous story, squad-based combat, extensive card variety, and rewarding progression systems create an experience that feels both accessible and strategically rich. While some players may wish for additional polish or greater narrative depth, the game's inventive premise and engaging gameplay more than compensate. For fans of deckbuilders and roguelikes looking for something with a unique personality, Union of Gnomes offers an entertaining and memorable adventure that stands out in a crowded genre. Rating: 8/10

After 10 hours, I felt like it was not very interesting or even much fun. The runs felt the same as there really isn't any need to adjust your deck once you get the hand of things. Well, until you hit a wall with some enemy that negates your deck completely thus wasting the entire run. The cards that are unlocked aren't typically any better than the starting set. The "Bling" accessories are only good for the current mission and are used up afterwards. Bling itself is hard to obtain as well. Meta-progression requires way too much grind for me to waste my time to do so. I feel the developers made the bad decision to stretch out the game play time with a very boring grinding mechanic. The story just wasn't for me. I didn't find any humor in it even though they tried nailing it to me with a big hammer. It was just over the top nonsense. The graphics are mediocre and the music is a very standard type. I came across a few bugs here and there. One time I went into an event mission inside the run and it wiped out all my money and sausages. It made it rather difficult to complete the overall run. Another time, the "shopoholics" didn't give me back the money they took after the battle which left me with no currency. It was then I decided that the game wasn't fun and just a tedious mess. While Union of Gnomes certainly isn't the worse card based battler I have played, there are far better once out there, I'm not going to waste any more time on this one. I'd say you can safely ignore this game and go buy something else.
